projects.name: IBM Connections Toolbar for Firefox
portfolio: A Firefox extension that let people search and use IBM Connections from the toolbar without navigating to it first. He co-created it with two colleagues at an IBM Hackday in 2010; it was built outside project work, and was released through OpenNTF under Apache 2.0 so it could reach users beyond the team that made it.
It reached over 6,000 users across IBM and enterprise customers, and was voted People's Innovation Choice by IBM employees globally. The repository and the OpenNTF project page are both still live.

projects.name: uCommand
portfolio: IBM UrbanCode Deploy shipped a command-line tool that automated some common tasks and left a lot missing. uCommand closed that gap: creating versions of artifacts, instantiating installs, and selecting which version to install.

Two of the choices are worth more than the tool. It was written in PHP because that was the common language on the team, not the language its author might have preferred. And it was a command-line tool so that teams beyond SalesConnect could pick it up.
It outlived its architect's departure and a handover to teams on another continent.
projects.tagline: Deployment command-line interface (CLI) closing the gaps in IBM UrbanCode Deploy

projects.name: gSmith
portfolio: gSmith's agents share a set of knowledge modules, splitting domain knowledge from agent behaviour so the rules live in one versioned source instead of being duplicated across prompts. A contract test suite fails the build when section citations, the roster or declared skills drift.

Inference cost is managed by tiering models to the task: mechanical compliance review on a cheap model, judgment-based review on Sonnet. One review pass is split into a cheap mechanical gate that runs the linters and an expensive judgment gate.
A module that would have taken a week to write and review could be done in a day, depending on complexity.
projects.tagline: Curriculum authoring and review toolkit, Claude Code

projects.name: Vita
portfolio: An AI assistant for job applications, running in Claude Code, built for the contractors at the BriX partnership to write and tailor a CV, cover letter and LinkedIn profile. It writes only from what each person has actually done, so nothing goes on the page that they could not back up in an interview. The owner and every contractor in the partnership use it.

I evaluated changes to the agent with pre-registered, blind-graded A/B experiments, confirming one that cut its starting context by more than half and catching a confidentiality defect that a fix then kept out of every final output in a retest.

Its criteria are not invented, and each rule carries the evidence for it: marked as evidenced with its source, as convention where nothing has been measured, or as contested where sound evidence disagrees. A rule whose stated reason collapses is withdrawn rather than left borrowing authority it no longer has.
A LinkedIn profile gets no score at all, because no scoring rubric for one has ever been validated, and saying so is more useful than inventing a number.

projects.name: jest-cucumber-fusion
portfolio: An open-source npm package that lets a team write Cucumber feature files and run them inside an ordinary Jest run, coverage included. The original package had been archived, and the library it was built on had gone more than a year without a release, while the dependencies they pulled in collected known vulnerabilities.

Rather than patch around a library he did not control, he took over the package and rebuilt it directly on the official Cucumber parsers, using the nWave AI-agent delivery method. Teams keep their feature files and step definitions in shape, change the import name, and follow a short documented migration.
Beyond what Jest itself brings, the vulnerable packages it adds to a project went from 12, one of them critical, to zero (npm audit, October 2026).
It is published on npm as @g_package/jest-cucumber-fusion; the unscoped name still belongs to B-Yond's original package.
projects.tagline: Open-source npm package, Cucumber tests in Jest
